verdict_reason: Faithful to the explicitly declared C=1 Ledoit-Wolf adaptation: deriving d(x)=sqrt((x-mu)^T Sigma_LW^+ (x-mu)), with S=(X-mu)^T(X-mu)/n and Sigma_LW=(1-alpha)S+alpha*trace(S)/d*I, gives independent moment/quadratic-form agreement to 4.3521e-14 relative on synthetic and real-model inputs, and the analytic cube gives sqrt(14)=3.741657386774 exactly at unit scale. Fixture integrity was checked using on_grid_translation (comparing its returned baseline), scale_ladder, degenerate_spectra, wide_dynamic_range, centring_is_safe and narrowing_is_safe: the unpatched evaluate() path returns finite results at all 7 requested scales from 1e-30 through 2.406159650500376e38 with AUROC exactly 0.391360, while a lossless +1e6 translation has maximum distance drift 8.78881e-11 and score-order rho=1.000000; 19 focused tests also pass.
comparable_reason: Raw distance is dominated by ambient width under a fixed isotropic null: d=64/128/256/512/1024 at n_fit=25 gives mean 8.168607119 -> 34.450445720 (4.217420x; Spearman rho=1.000000). The named squared-distance/d outputs remove the leading isotropic sqrt(d) growth but retain 1.050252101 -> 1.159546339 drift; exact zero-padding of a fixed 16-dimensional geometry to d=256 instead sends this statistic 0.898834019 -> 0.109045313 (-87.8681%, rho=-1.000000; pairwise-distance change 0.000e+00), so normalization is RED as a general cross-model calibration. AUROC is a separate, dimensionless ranking statistic: fresh matched-protocol GPT-2/Pythia-70M give 0.984320/0.680320, unchanged across 7 scale rungs for each model; five-split averaging reduces their 20-seed sample SD from 0.024749558/0.049019077 to 0.010374109/0.021769509, but does not calibrate covariance or corruption across models.
